items.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
items.abstract: ACCRUE is a continual off-policy reinforcement learning framework designed to improve robot foundation models. It addresses the challenge of learning new tasks while retaining past knowledge by carrying lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks. This allows for efficient reuse of learned behaviors and value functions, with a distillation mechanism to preserve prior task performance.
items.figure_caption: Single-task vs Continual off-policy RL. Single-task RL resets the actor and critic for each task, requiring repeated online interactions. Our method inherits both networks and uses small prior-task replay to accelerate learning while retaining prior performance.

items.title: Beyond Answer Voting: Fine-Grained Correction of LLM Reasoning through Graph Alignment across Sampled Traces
items.abstract: This paper introduces DDRG, a framework that goes beyond simple answer voting to fine-tune Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning.

items.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract: BLADE is a training-free framework for attributing failures in LLM multi-agent systems by auditing information use, not just tracing dependencies. It identifies critical "handoffs" between agents and assesses whether the information received was used faithfully and within task constraints, distinguishing between error introduction, propagation, and repair. This allows for more precise identification of the root cause of failures.

items.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for LLM agents to predict their own future failures by calibrating their confidence against the eventual success or failure of an entire task, rather than just the immediate action. By using outcome-grounded confidence calibration within a GRPO framework, the agent learns to better assess its reliability over multi-step episodes. This significantly improves the accuracy of its self-confidence signals, leading to substantially higher success rates for actions it deems most reliable.

items.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization
items.abstract: DPOison-VL is the first clean preference poisoning attack against Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization (VLM-DPO). It manipulates model alignment by introducing imperceptible perturbations to a small fraction of training images, leaving prompts, responses, and annotations unchanged. The attack uses bilevel optimization and a gradient alignment surrogate to efficiently steer image perturbations, and a preference displacement score for principled poison selection.
items.figure_caption: Overview of DPOison-VL . The pipeline consists of three stages: (S1) on-policy response generation, (S2) poison crafting, and (S3) poison selection, collectively steering DPO training toward target preference inversion.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents) that bridge the gap between internal latent reasoning and external text-based interaction. Their core method involves a novel architecture with a "HybridLink" that seamlessly transitions between text and latent modes, supported by a continuous working memory. This allows agents to leverage the efficiency of latent thought while retaining tool access and making their reasoning transparent, a significant contribution to building more capable and understandable AI agents.

items.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces ProAS, a framework for multi-turn reinforcement learning with LLM agents that addresses the uniform credit assignment problem in critic-free methods. ProAS uses an Agentic Reference Graph to dynamically shape advantages, masking unreasonable incentives and redistributing penalties to enable fine-grained credit assignment without a critic. This approach significantly improves the performance of existing group-based baselines.
items.figure_caption: (a) The demonstration of ARG. Diverse successful trajectories are unified into a DAG that serves as a progress reference. (b) Probing unreasonable actions. From an identical state, the counterpart injected with unreasonable actions yields a lower Expected Success Rate (ESR) on 50 sampled continuations { c i } i = 1 50 \{c_{i}\}_{i=1}^{50} . (c) Suppressing by Future-Drift (FD). Forcibly suppressing the original action at different trajectory points and resampling 50 continuations shows recovered ESR rises with the suppressed action’s FD.

items.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics
items.abstract: SEAR is a framework and benchmark that enables language-model agents to autonomously improve robot control by writing, testing, and retaining code as skills. Its core contribution is to rigorously evaluate whether these agents are truly learning and transferring knowledge across different environments and tasks, rather than simply iterating through random attempts. SEAR introduces novel controls and evaluation modes to isolate genuine learning from other factors, providing a more robust assessment of agentic robotics.

items.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Self-Evolving Agent Harness," a method that allows AI agents to improve their own software scaffolding (like prompts and tools) without retraining the underlying model. The core contribution is a feedback-driven, evolutionary optimization process that enables persistent, self-directed agent improvement, formally analyzed for reliability and generalization. This framework has implications for creating more robust and adaptable AI systems in various domains.
items.figure_caption: From reusable instructions and procedures to revisable executable components.

items.title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
items.abstract: SkillScaffold addresses the challenge of effectively integrating textual skills into agentic reinforcement learning for LLMs. Its core method involves a policy-adaptive training scaffold that efficiently estimates skill utility using outcome-aware likelihood comparisons and selectively injects beneficial skills. This approach improves exploration and learning by avoiding costly rollout-based evaluations and adapting skill usage to the current policy's competence.
items.figure_caption: Overview and empirical summary of SkillScaffold . Low-cost, policy-relative skill-utility estimates guide selective skill injection during training, while inference remains skill-free. Across four agentic benchmarks, SkillScaffold consistently outperforms GRPO and SkillRL while injecting skills for only a small fraction of training queries.

items.title: AgentStripes: An Evidence-Graded Maturity Model for AI Agents
items.abstract: AgentStripes is an evidence-graded maturity model for AI agents that goes beyond task performance to assess their reliability, safety, and observability. It defines seven levels of maturity, each gated by basic, safety, and proof requirements, and uses a structured system of capability ratings and evidence grades to deterministically calculate an agent's stripe level. The core contribution is a quantifiable and auditable framework for evaluating the engineering quality and trustworthiness of AI agents.

items.title: Auditing Future-Memory Use in Point-in-Time Language Agents
items.abstract: This paper investigates how point-in-time (PIT) language agents recall information beyond their training cutoff. The core method involves probing agents with historical company comparison tasks, then observing if they favor the better-remembered company when provided with PIT-valid evidence. The contribution is demonstrating that while agents can recall "future" facts, this recall doesn't necessarily predict their evidence gathering behavior in these specific tasks.

items.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
items.abstract: This paper introduces a method for LLMs to act as "agentic verifiers" for code, going beyond simple pass/fail judgments. The core method involves training an LLM (ARBITER) to diagnose code correctness and generate verifiable counterexamples using only the problem statement and candidate code. This contributes a novel approach to providing informative feedback for code generation and debugging, particularly in competitive programming contexts where official feedback is limited.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of Arbiter with an online judge ( left ) and the IOI 2026 case study ( right ). Under the same 50-submission cap per problem, the expected Arbiter score crosses the gold threshold in round 4; the expected online-judge-feedback score remains below it.

items.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
items.abstract: DoubtLess is a training-free decoding method that uses a smaller "brief thinker" model to guide a larger reasoning model towards generating shorter chains of thought. The brief thinker analyzes the large model's current output twice, once aiming for brevity and once for verbosity, and the difference in their predictions is used to steer the large model towards conciseness. This approach significantly reduces token usage in complex reasoning tasks without sacrificing accuracy, as demonstrated on various benchmarks.

items.title: From Relation-Specific Heads to Shared Interventions: Contextual Entrainment in Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates contextual entrainment in language models, where irrelevant tokens from earlier context can negatively impact later responses. The authors propose that instead of being relation-specific, the mechanisms driving entrainment involve shared components across different relations. By identifying and ablating specific attention heads, they demonstrate that interventions can recover model performance, with some heads showing transferable benefits across related tasks.

items.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: GeoReader addresses vision-language models' difficulty with spatial reasoning by explicitly teaching them to understand geometry. It trains lightweight "Geometric Readers" to translate geometric information into a format the VLM can already process, then fine-tunes the VLM to utilize this injected geometry for spatial question answering. This approach ensures geometry is not just captured but actively used by the VLM.
items.figure_caption: Geo Reader learns geometry in a form the receiving VLM can read. (a) QA-only fusion learns to use geometry through answer supervision. (b) Feature alignment matches VLM-generated representations to external geometry features. (c) Geo Reader first trains Geometric Readers through description prediction by a frozen VLM, then freezes the Readers and trains the VLM for QA. All three routes estimate geometry from RGB, which also directly conditions each VLM. Flames and ice cubes mark trainable and frozen modules. The pictured I 1 , I 2 , I 3 I_{1},I_{2},I_{3} are input views; the scene and answer are illustrative. Fig. 2 details the architecture.

items.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime for long-horizon agents. Instead of relying on interaction histories, CarryOn organizes context around reusable "task objects" representing progress. Its core contribution is a method to efficiently update these reusable objects when the surrounding history is retired, without full reconstruction, by maintaining and revising carrier records.
items.figure_caption: Context folding with reusable task objects in long-horizon OSWorld2.0 ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Top: In a slide-editing task, the working presentation and exported images carry completed editing progress, while remaining constraints and save verification stay explicit, reducing active context from 42.4K to 14.4K tokens (66.0%). Bottom: In a lab-report task, the working document carries completed edits, while unresolved calculations remain explicit, reducing active context from 58.4K to 23.5K tokens (59.7%).

items.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
items.abstract: This paper introduces the "Scenario-Actor" framework, a novel method for selecting LLM decoding temperature. Instead of fixed heuristics, it geometrically represents the communicative scenario using Transformer hidden states to infer situational characteristics. This approach adapts LLM generation to better suit interactive social scenarios and instruction following.

items.title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: This paper reveals that projector training in multimodal LLMs primarily achieves a coarse alignment, with most performance gains realized using only a small fraction of the data. Projectors trained on different datasets can be linearly interpolated, suggesting their specific details are less critical. Motivated by this, the authors propose PORTAL, a training-free initialization method that uses per-modality summary statistics and optimal transport to map Gaussian approximations of vision and language embeddings.
items.figure_caption: Projector alignment as a coarse alignment with a broad solution space. ( Left ) Standard pipeline: during projector alignment, the vision encoder and language model are frozen, and only the projector is trained to map visual tokens into a representation space compatible with the LLM using image-caption pairs. ( Middle ) We show that projectors trained on different image-caption datasets can be linearly interpolated while largely preserving downstream performance, indicating that there is a large solution space for the weights of the projector. ( Right ) This observation motivates a closed-form solution of projector alignment. We propose a training-free projector PORTAL constructed by optimal transport between the two modalities’ marginal statistics.

items.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
items.abstract: This paper introduces SolBehave, a benchmark for evaluating the behavioral correctness of LLM-generated smart contracts. Its core contribution is a novel synthetic-transaction replay method guided by a Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graph, which systematically tests legitimate function call sequences. This approach moves beyond simple compilation checks to ensure generated contracts behave as intended, addressing the critical issue of unpatchable errors in deployed smart contracts.

From an identical state, the counterpart injected with unreasonable actions yields a lower Expected Success Rate (ESR) on 50 sampled continuations { c i } i = 1 50 \{c_{i}\}_{i=1}^{50} . (c) Suppressing by Future-Drift (FD). Forcibly suppressing the original action at different trajectory points and resampling 50 continuations shows recovered ESR rises with the suppressed action’s FD.

papers.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics
papers.abstract: SEAR is a framework and benchmark that enables language-model agents to autonomously improve robot control by writing, testing, and retaining code as skills. Its core contribution is to rigorously evaluate whether these agents are truly learning and transferring knowledge across different environments and tasks, rather than simply iterating through random attempts. SEAR introduces novel controls and evaluation modes to isolate genuine learning from other factors, providing a more robust assessment of agentic robotics.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Self-Evolving Agent Harness," a method that allows AI agents to improve their own software scaffolding (like prompts and tools) without retraining the underlying model. The core contribution is a feedback-driven, evolutionary optimization process that enables persistent, self-directed agent improvement, formally analyzed for reliability and generalization. This framework has implications for creating more robust and adaptable AI systems in various domains.
papers.figure_caption: From reusable instructions and procedures to revisable executable components.

papers.title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
papers.abstract: SkillScaffold addresses the challenge of effectively integrating textual skills into agentic reinforcement learning for LLMs. Its core method involves a policy-adaptive training scaffold that efficiently estimates skill utility using outcome-aware likelihood comparisons and selectively injects beneficial skills. This approach improves exploration and learning by avoiding costly rollout-based evaluations and adapting skill usage to the current policy's competence.
papers.figure_caption: Overview and empirical summary of SkillScaffold . Low-cost, policy-relative skill-utility estimates guide selective skill injection during training, while inference remains skill-free. Across four agentic benchmarks, SkillScaffold consistently outperforms GRPO and SkillRL while injecting skills for only a small fraction of training queries.

papers.title: AgentStripes: An Evidence-Graded Maturity Model for AI Agents
papers.abstract: AgentStripes is an evidence-graded maturity model for AI agents that goes beyond task performance to assess their reliability, safety, and observability. It defines seven levels of maturity, each gated by basic, safety, and proof requirements, and uses a structured system of capability ratings and evidence grades to deterministically calculate an agent's stripe level. The core contribution is a quantifiable and auditable framework for evaluating the engineering quality and trustworthiness of AI agents.

papers.title: Auditing Future-Memory Use in Point-in-Time Language Agents
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how point-in-time (PIT) language agents recall information beyond their training cutoff. The core method involves probing agents with historical company comparison tasks, then observing if they favor the better-remembered company when provided with PIT-valid evidence. The contribution is demonstrating that while agents can recall "future" facts, this recall doesn't necessarily predict their evidence gathering behavior in these specific tasks.

papers.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method for LLMs to act as "agentic verifiers" for code, going beyond simple pass/fail judgments. The core method involves training an LLM (ARBITER) to diagnose code correctness and generate verifiable counterexamples using only the problem statement and candidate code. This contributes a novel approach to providing informative feedback for code generation and debugging, particularly in competitive programming contexts where official feedback is limited.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of Arbiter with an online judge ( left ) and the IOI 2026 case study ( right ). Under the same 50-submission cap per problem, the expected Arbiter score crosses the gold threshold in round 4; the expected online-judge-feedback score remains below it.

papers.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
papers.abstract: DoubtLess is a training-free decoding method that uses a smaller "brief thinker" model to guide a larger reasoning model towards generating shorter chains of thought. The brief thinker analyzes the large model's current output twice, once aiming for brevity and once for verbosity, and the difference in their predictions is used to steer the large model towards conciseness. This approach significantly reduces token usage in complex reasoning tasks without sacrificing accuracy, as demonstrated on various benchmarks.

papers.title: From Relation-Specific Heads to Shared Interventions: Contextual Entrainment in Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates contextual entrainment in language models, where irrelevant tokens from earlier context can negatively impact later responses. The authors propose that instead of being relation-specific, the mechanisms driving entrainment involve shared components across different relations. By identifying and ablating specific attention heads, they demonstrate that interventions can recover model performance, with some heads showing transferable benefits across related tasks.

papers.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: GeoReader addresses vision-language models' difficulty with spatial reasoning by explicitly teaching them to understand geometry. It trains lightweight "Geometric Readers" to translate geometric information into a format the VLM can already process, then fine-tunes the VLM to utilize this injected geometry for spatial question answering. This approach ensures geometry is not just captured but actively used by the VLM.
papers.figure_caption: Geo Reader learns geometry in a form the receiving VLM can read. (a) QA-only fusion learns to use geometry through answer supervision. (b) Feature alignment matches VLM-generated representations to external geometry features. (c) Geo Reader first trains Geometric Readers through description prediction by a frozen VLM, then freezes the Readers and trains the VLM for QA. All three routes estimate geometry from RGB, which also directly conditions each VLM. Flames and ice cubes mark trainable and frozen modules. The pictured I 1 , I 2 , I 3 I_{1},I_{2},I_{3} are input views; the scene and answer are illustrative. Fig. 2 details the architecture.

papers.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime for long-horizon agents. Instead of relying on interaction histories, CarryOn organizes context around reusable "task objects" representing progress. Its core contribution is a method to efficiently update these reusable objects when the surrounding history is retired, without full reconstruction, by maintaining and revising carrier records.
papers.figure_caption: Context folding with reusable task objects in long-horizon OSWorld2.0 ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Top: In a slide-editing task, the working presentation and exported images carry completed editing progress, while remaining constraints and save verification stay explicit, reducing active context from 42.4K to 14.4K tokens (66.0%). Bottom: In a lab-report task, the working document carries completed edits, while unresolved calculations remain explicit, reducing active context from 58.4K to 23.5K tokens (59.7%).

papers.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the "Scenario-Actor" framework, a novel method for selecting LLM decoding temperature. Instead of fixed heuristics, it geometrically represents the communicative scenario using Transformer hidden states to infer situational characteristics. This approach adapts LLM generation to better suit interactive social scenarios and instruction following.

papers.title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper reveals that projector training in multimodal LLMs primarily achieves a coarse alignment, with most performance gains realized using only a small fraction of the data. Projectors trained on different datasets can be linearly interpolated, suggesting their specific details are less critical. Motivated by this, the authors propose PORTAL, a training-free initialization method that uses per-modality summary statistics and optimal transport to map Gaussian approximations of vision and language embeddings.
papers.figure_caption: Projector alignment as a coarse alignment with a broad solution space. ( Left ) Standard pipeline: during projector alignment, the vision encoder and language model are frozen, and only the projector is trained to map visual tokens into a representation space compatible with the LLM using image-caption pairs. ( Middle ) We show that projectors trained on different image-caption datasets can be linearly interpolated while largely preserving downstream performance, indicating that there is a large solution space for the weights of the projector. ( Right ) This observation motivates a closed-form solution of projector alignment. We propose a training-free projector PORTAL constructed by optimal transport between the two modalities’ marginal statistics.

papers.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SolBehave, a benchmark for evaluating the behavioral correctness of LLM-generated smart contracts. Its core contribution is a novel synthetic-transaction replay method guided by a Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graph, which systematically tests legitimate function call sequences. This approach moves beyond simple compilation checks to ensure generated contracts behave as intended, addressing the critical issue of unpatchable errors in deployed smart contracts.
